correctness.rationale: For a centered Minkowski sum of two segments, the exact projection identity is \(W=a|\cos t|+b|\cos(t-\phi)|\). Integration gives \(\mu=2(a+b)/\pi\), \(\nu=(a^2+b^2)/2+2ab[\sin\phi+(\pi/2-\phi)\cos\phi]/\pi\); the maximum is the longer diagonal. Cancellation yields \(T=\tfrac12-(\sin\phi-\phi\cos\phi)/(\pi(1-\cos\phi))\), where the auxiliary ratio has derivative \(F^{\prime}(\phi)=\sin\phi(\phi-\sin\phi)/(1-\cos\phi)^2>0\). Thus the angle and unordered side lengths recover uniquely from monotone inversion and a nonnegative quadratic discriminant. Positive compact lower bounds make the angle and side-product maps Lipschitz; the square-root extraction is uniformly \(1/2\)-Hölder and the family \((a,b)=(1+t,1-t)\) makes that exponent sharp. The finite verification program does not establish infinite quantifiers; flattened parallelograms are excluded.

originality.rationale: A complete comparison against the identified initiating projection-distribution work, the square-width moments, and a later quadrilateral chord law found no coverage of the three-statistic rigidity or the sharp 1/2 inverse-stability theorem. The source for unconstrained symmetric planar bodies gives nonuniqueness in a larger class, not uniqueness in this three-parameter parallelogram class. Historical rediscovery as a classical perimeter, quadratic width, and diameter invariant remains a nontrivial residual risk; novelty is not inferred merely from missing search hits.
residual_risks: Equivalent classical results expressed via perimeter, quadratic mean width, and diameter rather than probability distribution may predate the indexed searches.
Uninspected literature or unpublished work outside available source and database coverage could contain a stronger determination theorem.

value.rationale: A natural inverse geometric-tomography question—recovering a three-parameter parallelogram despite erasing measurement directions—has a complete explicit answer from just three scalar measurements. The strict angle map supplies a usable constructive invariant, with rectangular equality and sharp inverse-conditioning boundary at equal sides. This goes beyond recomputation of the square moments. It is intrinsically meaningful for orientation-unlabeled width data; no arbitrary slice or unsupported downstream claim is required.
